title: Distinct Blocks of Length k

concept.title: A set of all substrings of one length
body: A **substring** is a block of consecutive letters. A word of length `n` has `n - k + 1` substrings of length `k`, and several of them may be equal. To count the different ones, put them all into a set and take its size.

body.code:
distinct = set()
for i in range(len(s) - k + 1):
    distinct.add(s[i:i + k])
print(len(distinct))

body: Every substring is copied (`k` letters) and hashed (also `k` steps), so the work is `O((n - k + 1) * k)`. This is fine for small `k`; for large `k` clever tricks (rolling hash, suffix structures) avoid copying, and you will meet them later.

statement: Given a word and a number `k`, count how many different blocks of exactly `k` consecutive letters the word contains.
inputFormat: The second line has the word.
outputFormat: Print the number of different blocks.

examples.note: The blocks are ab, bc, ca, ab, bc: three different ones.

hints: The word has `length - k + 1` blocks of length k.
Put every block into a set.
The answer is the size of the set.

explanation: All blocks of length `k` go into a hash set; its size is the number of different blocks.
solution.complexity: Time O(n * k) on average, space O(n * k).

code.python:
k = int(input())
s = input().strip()

distinct = set()
for i in range(len(s) - k + 1):
    distinct.add(s[i:i + k])
print(len(distinct))
